mainTopic: How a corpse's limb, bone and grave make a person טמא; when a טמא נזיר starts counting again; and the kinds of טומאה for which a נזיר does not shave
overview: The amud opens with a known rule: טומאה inside a sealed grave bursts straight up and straight down. רב יהודה then quotes a ברייתא that explains, word by word, the פסוק in במדבר 19:18 about touching a bone, the slain, the dead, or a grave. ריש לקיש explains that 'grave' means an old grave from before the Torah was given. The גמרא tries to use the word 'מת' (a limb from a corpse) as a proof for ריש לקיש. רבי יוחנן pushes the proof away by saying that word teaches טומאה through carrying. Next, the גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'until he becomes pure': sunset on day seven (רבי אליעזר) or bringing the קרבנות on day eight (רבנן). It proves from the next משנה's wording that it means after the קרבנות, as רבנן hold. Finally, a new משנה lists doubtful and other kinds of טומאה for which a נזיר does not shave, though in the cases from a dead body he is still sprinkled on the third and seventh days.

steps.title: Impurity bursts up and down from a sealed grave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its earlier point with a known teaching: טומאה inside a sealed grave bursts upward and downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: Impurity bursts through and goes up, and bursts through and goes down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known teaching to back up what it just said about a grave. Because the טומאה 'bursts through,' the grave itself makes things טמא like the dead body does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a dead body is sealed in a closed grave, the טומאה does not stay trapped inside. It 'breaks out' straight up and straight down, so whatever is directly above or below becomes טמא. This sets up the contrast with the next step, which deals with touching rather than this kind of spreading.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
Bursts through
Goes up / goes down

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Impurity bursts through and goes up,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a body sealed inside a closed grave. The טומאה breaks out of the sealed space.

phrases.english: bursts through and goes down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the point the גמרא was making just before this section about a grave's טומאה.
steps.raayaObject: That a sealed grave passes on טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known teaching quoted as 'אמר מר': טומאה bursts up and down

steps.title: A ברייתא explains bone, slain, and dead in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes a ברייתא that explains the words of במדבר 19:18 about touching: a bone the size of a barley grain, a limb cut from a living person, and a limb cut from a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding touching, רב יהודה said that a ברייתא teaches: 'Whoever touches a bone or the slain.' 'A bone' means a bone the size of a barley grain. 'Or the slain' means a limb cut off from a living person that does not have enough flesh to heal. 'Or the dead' means a limb cut off from a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from טומאה that spreads to טומאה by touching. It quotes a ברייתא that explains each word of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק is given its own meaning. 'Bone' means even a small bone, the size of a barley grain. 'Slain' (חלל) means a limb cut from a living person, and 'dead' (מת) means a limb cut from a corpse. The word 'מת' is the one the גמרא will use as a proof in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching
A bone the size of a barley grain
A limb cut off from a living person
To heal (literally, to bring up a cure)

phrases.english: Whereas regarding touching,
Rav Yehuda said that it was taught in a baraita:
"(And all) who touch a bone or the slain"
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:18. Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.english: "A bone": this is a bone the size of a barley grain,

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹ בֶחָלָל״ — זֶה אֵבֶר הַנֶחְלָל מִן הַחַי
phrases.english: "Or the slain": this is a limb cut off from a living person
that does not have enough flesh to heal,

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹ בְּמֵת״ — זֶה אֵבֶר הַנֶחְלָל מִן הַמֵּת,
phrases.english: "Or the dead": this is a limb cut off from a dead body,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ גַּבֵּי נְגִיעָה, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: step 1 was about טומאה spreading from a grave, and this step is about touching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each word in the פסוק teaches a separate source of טומאה by touching: a barley-grain bone, a limb from a living person, and a limb from a dead body.

steps.title: ריש לקיש explains which grave the פסוק means
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the 'grave' in the פסוק is a grave from before the Torah was given.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or a grave': ריש לקיש said: this is a grave from before the Torah was given.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches the last word of the פסוק, 'grave,' and ריש לקיש explains what kind of grave it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says the word 'grave' here means an old grave, from before the Torah and its laws of טומאה were given. Such a grave makes a person טמא when he touches it. It does not make him טמא by being under the same roof (אהל).

keyTerms.meaning: A grave
From before the Torah was given (literally, before the Speech)

phrases.english: "Or a grave":
Reish Lakish said:
This is a grave from before the Speech.
phrases.notes: 'The Speech' means when ה׳ gave the Torah and these laws. So this is a grave from before then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the word-by-word reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'grave' in the פסוק is a grave from before the Torah was given, and it makes things טמא by touching.

steps.title: A limb from a corpse must mean one without a barley-grain bone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case 'a limb from a dead body' could be. If it has a barley-grain bone, it is already covered by 'bone.' So it must have no such bone, and the Torah still makes it a source of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This limb from a dead body, what is the case? If it has a bone the size of a barley grain, that is already 'whoever touches a bone'! Rather, it has no barley-grain bone, and even so the Torah included it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the word 'מת' in the ברייתא as a proof for ריש לקיש's side against רבי יוחנן. It argues that the word cannot be repeating 'bone,' so it must teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that the Torah does not repeat itself. A limb with a barley-grain bone is already covered by the word 'bone,' so 'מת' must mean a limb without such a bone. That shows the Torah treats this limb strictly even though it is missing something, which helps ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
That is the same as
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Included it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the ברייתא itself. The גמרא is using the ברייתא as a proof in the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת, הֵיכִי דָמֵי?
phrases.english: This limb from a dead body, what is the case?
If it has in it a bone the size of a barley grain,
that is the same as "whoever touches a bone"!
Rather, it does not have a bone the size of a barley grain,
and even so the Merciful One included it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת, הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the phrase 'אבר הנחלל מן המת' from the ברייתא in step 2 and builds a proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's position against רבי יוחנן about a limb from a corpse
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's separate word 'מת' cannot repeat 'bone,' so it must be a limb without a barley-grain bone, and the Torah still includes it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read so that it is not a repeat, the word 'מת' shows the Torah includes even a limb without a barley-grain bone.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the word teaches טומאה through carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the limb really does have a barley-grain bone. Since touching is already taught by 'bone,' the extra word teaches that carrying it also makes a person טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: Really, it does have a bone. If the word is not needed to teach about touching it, use it to teach about carrying it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes away the proof from step 4. He agrees the word is not a repeat, but he says it teaches a new law about carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 4 depended on the idea that the word 'מת' had to teach about a limb without a bone. רבי יוחנן finds another job for the word: it is the same limb with a bone, but it teaches טומאה by carrying (משא), not only by touching. So the word is not extra, and there is no proof for ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you; this gives a possible answer
Really, actually
If it is not needed for this matter, apply it to that matter
Touching / carrying

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'מת' in the פסוק does not prove ריש לקיש's view. רבי יוחנן reads it as a limb with a bone and uses it to teach טומאה by carrying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא answers a proof from an 'extra' word: it finds the word a different job, so the proof falls away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan can say to you:
Really, it does have a bone in it.
And if it is not needed for the matter of touching it,
phrases.notes: Touching a bone was already taught by the word 'bone,' so this word does not need to teach it again.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of carrying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 4 by giving the word 'מת' a different meaning.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof for ריש לקיש from the word 'מת.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the word had to mean a limb without a bone. It can mean a limb with a bone and teach the separate law of carrying.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה about sprinkling and losing the counted days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about a טמא נזיר being sprinkled on the third and seventh days and losing his earlier days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he is sprinkled on the third day and the seventh day, and he loses his earlier days, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה so it can ask a question about it. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who became טמא from a dead body gets the ashes of the פרה אדומה sprinkled on him on day three and day seven. He also loses the days of נזירות he already counted. The words 'and so on' point to the end of that line, 'until he becomes pure,' which the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkles, meaning the ashes of the פרה אדומה are sprinkled on the טמא person
Loses, or cancels, the days of נזירות he already counted
And so on, meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: And he sprinkles on the third and on the seventh day
phrases.notes: Someone who is טהור sprinkles water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה on the טמא נזיר.

phrases.english: and he loses his earlier days, and so on.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (as the setup of the question that follows)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the discussion of bones and limbs and goes back to the words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא נזיר is sprinkled on day three and day seven and loses his earlier days of נזירות.

steps.title: What does 'until he becomes pure' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'until he becomes pure' means the sunset of the seventh day (רבי אליעזר) or bringing the קרבנות on the eighth day (רבנן).
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The משנה says he does not start counting 'until he becomes pure.' Is it talking about the seventh day, meaning until the sun sets, so the משנה follows רבי אליעזר? Or is it talking about the eighth day, meaning until he brings his קרבנות, so the משנה follows רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question: which moment does 'until he becomes pure' point to? It gives two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: on day seven, once the sun sets, he is pure and starts counting again. That fits רבי אליעזר. Option two: he starts counting only on day eight, after he brings his קרבנות. That fits רבנן, who hold that the new נזירות does not start before that.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked, a real question the חכמים were unsure about
Until he becomes pure
Sunset, the waiting after טבילה until the sun goes down
His קרבנות, the offerings a טמא נזיר brings on the eighth day
And whose opinion is it?

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree he must wait. The only question is whether he starts counting at sunset on day seven or after the קרבנות on day eight.

phrases.english: They asked:
That which it teaches, 'until he becomes pure,'
is it talking about the seventh day,
meaning until he waits for sunset,
and whose view is it? It is רבי אליעזר.
Or perhaps it is talking about the eighth day,
and what does 'until he becomes pure' mean?
Until he brings his offerings.
And whose view is it? It is the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the end of the line just quoted from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'until he becomes pure' mean sunset of day seven (רבי אליעזר) or bringing the קרבנות on day eight (רבנן)?

steps.title: The next משנה proves it means after the קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: Because the next משנה says a different נזיר 'starts counting immediately,' the different wording here must mean later: after bringing the קרבנות, which is the view of רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the next part says 'he starts counting right away.' So the first part, 'until he becomes pure,' must mean until he brings his קרבנות. That is רבנן, who say a pure נזירות does not start before the eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by comparing the wording of this משנה with the wording of the next one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the cases in the next משנה, where no קרבנות are brought, it says 'he starts counting right away,' meaning once his seven days are over. If our משנה meant the same moment, it would have used the same words. Since it says 'until he becomes pure' instead, it must mean a later point, after the קרבנות on day eight, as רבנן hold.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
The first part of the משנה
He starts counting right away
Does not take effect

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבנן: a נזיר who became טמא starts his new pure נזירות only after he brings his קרבנות on the eighth day.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
from the fact that the later part teaches:
phrases.notes: This is the next משנה, about doubtful טומאה where he doesn't shave or bring קרבנות.

phrases.english: 'he starts and counts right away,'
then in the first part, what does 'until he becomes pure' mean?
Until he brings his offerings,
and whose view is it? It is the רבנן, who say:

phrases.aramaic: נְזִירוּת דְּטׇהֳרָה עַד שְׁמִינִי לָא חָיְילָא.
phrases.english: a נזירות of purity does not take effect until the eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by choosing the second option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Until he becomes pure' means until he brings his קרבנות; the משנה follows רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'מַתְחִיל וּמוֹנֶה מִיָּד' in the next משנה.

steps.title: New משנה: doubtful kinds of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins, listing cases of doubtful טומאה: overhanging branches, sticking-out stones, and a בית הפרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: But overhanging branches, sticking-out stones, and a בית הפרס...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It begins a list of cases that are different from the earlier list, and the list continues past these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה listed the kinds of טומאה for which a נזיר must shave. The word 'but' shows that these new cases are different: they are cases of doubt, and he does not shave for them. In each case we are not sure he was really under the טומאה of a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: Overhanging tree branches, where it is unclear which one is over a dead body
Stones sticking out of a wall, where it is unclear which one is over the טומאה
A field where a grave was plowed, so bones may be scattered in it

phrases.english: MISHNA: But the overhanging branches,
and the sticking-out stones, and a בית הפרס,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next משנה, which step 8 just used as its proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful cases of טומאה such as סככות, פרעות, and בית הפרס are listed apart from the cases where a נזיר shaves.

steps.title: The rest of the list, and the rule that the נזיר does not shave
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of lighter or doubtful טומאות and rules that for these the נזיר does not shave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also: the land outside ארץ ישראל, a grave's cover stone, a grave's side walls, a quarter-לוג of blood, a tent, a quarter-קב of bones, vessels that touched a dead body, and the days when he is a מצורע (counting days or full days). For all of these, the נזיר does not shave.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing cases that started in Step 9, then gives the main rule: for all of these, the נזיר does not shave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who becomes טמא from the sources in the earlier משנה must shave and start his נזירות over. The cases here are not on that list. Some are doubtful, like the overhanging branches, and some are rabbinic, like the land outside ארץ ישראל. Others, like the גולל, a רביעית of blood or a quarter-קב of bones, are simply not among the sources for which a נזיר shaves. The two מצורע cases are listed too: during those days he does not shave like a טמא מת.

keyTerms.meaning: Land outside ארץ ישראל, which the רבנן declared טמא
The cover stone of a grave and the side walls it rests on
A quarter-לוג of blood from a dead body
A quarter-קב of bones from a dead body
A מצורע's seven counting days after healing, and his days as a full מצורע
Shaves, as a טמא נזיר does to restart his נזירות

steps.confusionAlert: 'Does not shave' does not mean these cases have no effect at all. The משנה goes on right away to say that some of them still need sprinkling.

phrases.english: And the land of the nations,
phrases.notes: He means a נזיר who went outside ארץ ישראל. The רבנן declared that land טמא.

phrases.english: and the grave cover, and the grave walls,
and a quarter-log of blood, and a tent,
and a quarter-kav of bones,
and vessels that touch a corpse,
and in the days of his counting, and in the days of his full leprosy
phrases.notes: These two are about a נזיר who is a מצורע, not about טומאת מת.

phrases.english: for these the nazirite does not shave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of cases that began in Step 9 and gives the ruling for all of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For all the listed cases (doubtful, rabbinic, or simply not among the sources that require shaving), and for the days of צרעת, the נזיר does not shave.

steps.title: He is still sprinkled on the third and seventh days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins to explain what does happen in these cases: the נזיר still receives sprinkling on day three and day seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is sprinkled on the third day and on the seventh day,
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new part of its ruling. Even though he does not shave, he still has to be sprinkled, and the sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not shaving does not mean he is completely טהור. In the cases that involve טומאת מת, he still needs the normal purification of sprinkling on the third and seventh days. This sets up the next words of the משנה, which tell us what happens to the days he already counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkles the purifying water (of the פרה אדומה) on him
On the third and seventh days of his purification

phrases.english: and he is sprinkled on the third and on the seventh days,
phrases.notes: This only applies to the cases from a dead body, not to the מצורע days. The sentence keeps going after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling that he does not shave, the משנה starts to say what purification he still needs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the cases of טומאת מת on the list, the נזיר is still sprinkled on the third and seventh days.
